- [S0515] types=[DISTINCTION, EXTENSION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Corrects a model that would treat Person, Object, and Cause as equivalent node types: Person and Object are both entities/nodes but Person additionally carries agency, beliefs, desires, reasons, intentions, and action-capacity beyond Object's mere properties/capacities; Cause is not an entity at all but a relation/dependency type (e.g. Fire--causes-->heating, Person--causes-->intention), citing O'Connor's distinction between event causation and agent causation." (anchor: "Persons and objects are not merely two kinds of "things." Persons introduce agency, reasons, intentions, and causal powers into the space. Causes introduce directed dependency between things, states, events, and actions. ... Cause -> RELATION / DEPENDENCY")
- [S0515] types=[CONCEPT, FORMALIZATION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Formalizes O'Connor's causal-capacity structure for objects (Object->Properties->Causal capacity->[circumstances]->Effect) and agents (Person->{beliefs,desires,reasons}->Agent capacity->Intention->Action), illustrated by 'a person can open the door' requiring bodily capability+knowledge+desire+opportunity before capacity-to-act yields possible action; Capacity is identified as the bridge concept between what something is and what it can do." (anchor: "particulars have properties → properties ground causal capacities → capacities can be exercised → effects occur. ... capacity / capacity becomes an important bridge between WHAT SOMETHING IS and WHAT SOMETHING CAN DO.")
- [S0515] types=[EXTENSION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Chains reasons/beliefs/desires into a deliberation->intention->action sequence, arguing this lets KnowledgeOS represent 'why did it happen' as a distinct knowledge class from 'what happened', citing O'Connor's connection of actions to the agent's desire-belief complexes or reasons." (anchor: "Person -> believes X, desires Y, has reason R -> deliberation -> intention -> action ... KnowledgeOS can represent not just: what happened? but: why did it happen? That is a completely different class of knowledge.")
- [S0515] types=[HYPOTHESIS, EXAMPLE] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Decomposes 'Alice opened the door because she wanted to leave' into Person/Event/Object/Mental-State/Reason/Causal-Explanatory-Relation/Truth-bearer/Truth-status/Evidence/Source without any primitive 'Knowledge' object, concluding knowledge emerges from the structured configuration -- explicitly connected to Merricks' 'arranged-X-wise' eliminativism." (anchor: "KnowledgeOS doesn't necessarily need a primitive object called Knowledge. Instead it can represent: PERSON Alice, EVENT opening-the-door, ... REASON wanting-to-leave, CAUSAL/EXPLANATORY RELATION wanting-to-leave --explains--> opening-the-door, TRUTH-BEARER ... The knowledge emerges from the structured configuration.")
- [S0515] types=[PRINCIPLE, RESTATEMENT] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Combines Merricks' non-collapses (Truth≠evidence≠aboutness≠truthmaker) with five new O'Connor-derived non-collapses (Cause≠explanation, Person≠object, Reason≠cause, Action≠event-description, Capacity≠actual exercise) into the central converging principle: knowledge is not a primitive bucket containing facts, but structured intelligibility over different kinds of entities, states, events, relations, reasons, causes, and truth-bearers." (anchor: "Cause ≠ explanation, Person ≠ object, Reason ≠ cause, Action ≠ event-description, Capacity ≠ actual exercise. ... Knowledge is not a primitive bucket containing facts. Knowledge is structured intelligibility over different kinds of entities, states, events, relations, reasons, causes, and truth-bearers.")
- [S0515] types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Proposes two intersecting dimensions for the Knowledge Space instead of one hierarchy: Dimension A (particulars: objects/persons/events/states/situations vs universals: properties/capacities/powers/relations, citing O'Connor's particular/universal distinction) and Dimension B (fourteen relation types: identity, instantiation, part-of, about, causes, enables, prevents, depends-on, explains, supports, intends, believes, desires, acts-on), combined as Knowledge Space = Entities x Relations x States x Claims x Contexts." (anchor: "Dimension A — What exists / what we refer to (Particulars: Objects/Persons-Agents/Events/States/Situations; Universals/Properties: Properties/Capacities/Powers/Relations) ... Dimension B — How things are connected (identity, instantiation, part-of, about, causes, enables, prevents, depends-on, explains, supports, intends, believes, desires, acts-on) ... Knowledge Space = Entities × Relations × States × Claims × Contexts.")
- [S0515] types=[DISTINCTION, HYPOTHESIS] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Identifies Person as the bridge between ontology and epistemology, being simultaneously entity, bearer-of-properties, causal agent, source of reasons, holder of beliefs/intentions, actor, observer, knower, and producer of claims, so that WORLD->perception->PERSON->{belief,reasoning,intention,decision,action}->WORLD; concludes persons are participants that traverse and transform Knowledge Space, not merely objects inside it. (This claim is explicitly challenged as architectural 'overreach' later in this same file's Critical Analysis section.)" (anchor: "Persons are not merely objects inside Knowledge Space. They are participants that traverse and transform Knowledge Space. ... a person is simultaneously an entity + a bearer of properties + a causal agent + a source of reasons + a holder of beliefs + a holder of intentions + an actor + an observer + a knower + a producer of claims.")
- [S0515] types=[DISTINCTION, EXTENSION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Distinguishes CAUSE from EXPLANATION as separate KnowledgeOS concepts with relationships between them, since 'why X?' is not always identical to 'what caused X?', enumerating seven non-identical explanation kinds (physical, causal, functional, intentional, reasons, historical, logical) that must not be treated as the same thing, citing O'Connor's exploration of the relationship between causal and reasons-based explanation." (anchor: "humans don't merely ask: What caused X? They ask: Why X? Those aren't always identical. ... KnowledgeOS probably needs CAUSE and separately EXPLANATION, with relationships between them ... physical explanation, causal explanation, functional explanation, intentional explanation, reasons explanation, historical explanation, logical explanation ... without pretending they're all the same thing.")
- [S0515] types=[HYPOTHESIS, DEFINITION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "States the file's central research hypothesis: Knowledge Space is a relational space (nodes: entities/events/states/properties/propositions/mental contents; edges: identity/instantiation/aboutness/causation/explanation/dependence/support/intention/agency), not a hierarchy of topics; Topics become projections over this space rather than primitives, illustrated by 'Topic: Free Will' as a projection over Persons+Actions+Reasons+Intentions+Causes+Possibilities+Responsibility+Time+Truth-claims." (anchor: "Knowledge Space is not primarily a hierarchy of topics. It is a relational space whose nodes represent entities, events, states, properties, propositions and mental contents, while its edges represent relations such as identity, instantiation, aboutness, causation, explanation, dependence, support, intention and agency. Then topics become views over that space. Not primitives.")
- [S0515] types=[GOVERNANCE] scope=CROSS-OBJECT — "States three converging constraints from Merricks, O'Connor, and the project's own KnowledgeOS investigation, concluding the right next step is not to declare an ontology but to run a 'Knowledge Space Ontological Discovery' over 22 candidates (Persons, Objects, Properties, Events, States, Actions, Agents, Causes, Effects, Powers, Capacities, Reasons, Intentions, Claims, Propositions, Truth, Evidence, Sources, Contexts, Time, Modality, Explanation), asking of each whether it is a primitive entity, relation, property, state, representation, perspective, or merely a useful projection." (anchor: "Merricks: Truth cannot be reduced to truthmaking/evidence/aboutness. O'Connor: Persons, objects, properties, powers, causes, reasons, intentions and actions cannot simply be collapsed into events or objects. Our KnowledgeOS investigation: Knowledge must remain reconstructible, contextual, governed and evidentially traceable. ... Is this a primitive entity, a relation, a property, a state, a representation, a perspective, or merely a useful projection?")
- [S0515] types=[WARNING, CORRECTION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Warns against four dangers of importing O'Connor's framework uncritically: (1) treating Person/Agent Causation/Intention/Action as Kernel primitives would make the Kernel a metaphysical engine -- the Kernel should preserve records of agency, not implement agency; (2) the Kernel becoming an arbiter of what truly causes/explains what would make it a 'semantic oracle' -- it should preserve claims about explanation, not the explanations themselves (paralleling Assertion-preserved vs Truth-evaluated-externally); (3) capacities/powers are notoriously hard to formalize (counterfactuals, contexts, degrees, interactions) and belong in assertion content, not Kernel structure; (4) treating persons as active Kernel-level transformers of Knowledge Space is overreach -- the Kernel should preserve records of participation (who made what claim, when, based on what), not model transformative agency itself."
